claims: For CPMM integer swap output, the floor output is never above the ceiling output and the ceiling/floor gap is at most one unit per edge.
The per-edge CPMM rounding gap can be expressed in integer form as actual floor output greater than or equal to ideal ceiling output minus one.
An arbitrage certificate with margin at least one against ceiling-weight CPMM edges remains no-arbitrage safe under floor-rounded CPMM edges.
The complete CPMM graph instantiation provides the perturbation hypothesis directly from pool reserves and trade amounts.
Concrete witnesses cover ceiling division, tight gap-one behavior, exact gap-zero behavior, integer perturbation, certificate absorption, and end-to-end pathWeight behavior.

boundaries: The rounding theorem is per CPMM edge and uses a one-unit integer perturbation bound; multi-hop certificate margins must account for the chosen path/cycle model.
The no-arbitrage theorem assumes a provided potential certificate with margin at least one on ceiling weights.
The theorem does not prove that a runtime graph builder emits all relevant CPMM edges, nor that oracle-derived edge weights are fresh or authorized.
The packet is a math bridge from CPMM rounding to arbitrage-certificate safety, not a routing optimality or liquidity adequacy proof.
